summary: Investigate the round 85-86 CM550 leads (CM550/CM848 twins, misnamed functions, vocabulary, EMA filter records) and have a skeptic refute each proposal

changes.reason: TWIN of CM848 0x539938. Test used for pairs 1-3: every statement of the shorter function has a counterpart at the same position in the longer one, with the same constants, and the longer one only adds blocks. CM848 has 6 statements: completed power-down count + 1, queue the 2-byte EEPROM write, wait at most 1000 passes, power cycle sequence number = completed + incomplete, queue it, wait at most 1000 passes, then call the application main's restart entry through a register-loaded address. CM550 has all six in the same order, with 1000 and the same record offsets. It only adds blocks: the inline watchdog kicks, vp44_initVP44StatusMonitoring (it points the discrete-input override pointer and runs mc68k_sampleAndDebounceDiscreteInputs 4 times) and an interrupt mask that is restored before the jump. The per-pass delays are platform delays. The only hardware access is the watchdog kick, so the unprefixed shared name loses nothing.

changes.reason: TWIN of CM848 0x539d18 under the same test, with the caveats below. The CM848 function has 15 statements and all of them recur in CM550 in the same order with the same constants: development_mode = OFF, ram_refresh_enable = ENABLED, run_location = NORMAL; wait at most 1000 passes for the EEPROM write queue; call the power-down EEPROM save; write the key-on hour meter (4 bytes) and the engine hour meter (4 bytes), each with a wait of at most 1000; status = 0; change an output; 40 windows that check the key and, if it is on, change the output back and restart; change the output after the windows; 4 short delays; check the key and restart; status = 1; wait for the key and restart. CM550 adds blocks: jsr 0x30a5e, the parameter bank word copy, 4 calls to cm550_savePowerDownDataToFlashBank, cm550_updateBootBlockFromImage, the bit-2 latch handling and interrupt masks around the waits. Caveats: (1) 0x30a5e sets 0x208 status bits like CM848's cm848_flagTripInformationPowerDownDataLoss, but it runs inside the CM550 function, while CM848 runs its version in the caller just before the call. (2) The two EEPROM-save callees differ. CM848's saveEepromForPowerDown also writes the verify-retry total, the checksum and the completed sequence number. CM550's 0x27c20 writes only the mirror chunks, and its completed-sequence write (0x803fe4 <- 0x803fe2) is in cm550_savePowerDownDataToFlashBank, which still runs between the EEPROM save and the hour meters. (3) Matching the output change to CM848's logical output 27 is my inference from position: CM550 changes bit 3 of the byte at 0x80bcf8 and then calls mc68k_ioDriverStrobeHandler. Confidence is medium because of these caveats. If a reviewer counts the blocks only CM550 has as 'the code differs', fall back to counterparts and keep both names.

changes.reason: Both main_loop functions are the same thing, so one better shared name replaces the old one. Each is the periodic interrupt timer's handler: it runs one frame of a 40-phase executive and times it with the executive timing gatherer. It is not a loop, and the snake_case name also breaks the lowerCamelCase rule for functions. The CM550 one is the raw exception handler (movem save ... movem restore; rte) that the vector table points at. CM848's is a callback (blr) that the SIU dispatcher calls (see the CM848 row). The bodies have the same design. Phases 0-39 (0x27) wrap to 0, and the default case also sets 0. Every phase makes one common call, then alternates even and odd task sets, then calls rotating groups. The timing gatherer clears the 40 per-phase records when its enable switches on (total 0 / count 0 / minimum 0xffff / maximum 0 / overflow 0), takes the start time, updates maximum / minimum / total / count and the overflow counters after the phase, and steps the record pointer; phase 0 resets the pointer. The confidence rates that both are the same thing; the name is my choice (alternative: periodicExecutiveInterruptHandler). The old name survives in comments: 54 lines of the CM848 .cpp, 10 CM848 global comments and 9 CM848 function comments. It also survives in the phase globals main_loop_scheduler_phase (CM848 0x3fa008) and main_loop_iteration_counter / main_loop_phase_index / main_loop_reserved (CM550). Update them or add '(was main_loop)'.
